clue.text: Heinlein has old chap acquiring family

definitions.text: Heinlein has old chap acquiring family

parts.words: Heinlein has old chap acquiring family
parts.note: Robert Heinlein wrote a novel whose title is the Bible's oldest man plus his children, an old chap acquiring a family

explanation.surface: A remark about the writer Heinlein taking in an elderly man who gains relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Heinlein's novel is 'Methuselah's Children'; Methuselah, who lived 969 years in Genesis, is the old chap, and the children are the family he acquires.
explanation.definitionFit: The patriarch from Genesis, famous for his long life, gives his name to Heinlein's novel about long-lived families.

clue.text: Stricken Jordanian kingdom in Samoa, bewilderingly enough

indicators.note: the kingdom's name sits inside the run of letters across the words Samoa and bewilderingly

explanation.surface: A struck-down Middle Eastern kingdom turns up, puzzlingly, in a Pacific island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bewilderingly' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters simply run on across the word join. The biblical kingdom east of the Dead Sea, now in Jordan, is stricken in the prophecies of Isaiah and Jeremiah.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient biblical realm lay in what is now western Jordan and is laid waste in the Old Testament prophets.

clue.text: Cape territory composer

parts.note: a tippet is a short cape or stole worn over the shoulders
T is a standard abbreviation for territory

explanation.surface: A composer from the Cape region of South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape territory' reads as one place, the Cape Province, but splits into a garment and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Michael Tippett was an English composer, known for A Child of Our Time.

clue.text: A single heretical principle? (Defended by Priestley)

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, one of something
Arianism, the doctrine of Arius denying Christ's full divinity, was condemned as heresy

explanation.surface: Asking whether one heretical idea was the creed the scientist Joseph Priestley championed.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Priestley, the chemist who isolated oxygen, was also a leading Unitarian minister; the whole clue nods to the faith's own denial of the Trinity.
explanation.definitionFit: Priestley preached and wrote for the creed denying the Trinity, so the belief system is the one he defended.

clue.text: Feature new dramatist in Wuthering Heights

parts.note: an ear is a facial feature
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A new playwright's touch appearing in Emily Bronte's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a family name found in the novel: Catherine and Hindley Earnshaw live at Wuthering Heights.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine, Hindley and Hareton of that surname are central figures of Emily Bronte's novel, owners of the house itself.

clue.text: God offers nothing on a vote for spacecraft

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: a poll is a vote
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A deity offering nothing more than a ballot when spaceships are concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: The god's name was given to NASA's moon programme, so 'for spacecraft' says the name also serves the craft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek and Roman deity of light, music and prophecy, whose name NASA borrowed for its lunar missions.

clue.text: An average match for Henry VIII, we're told

indicators.note: says the word for average is heard, standing for a surname spelt differently

parts.note: par is an average or normal level

explanation.surface: Someone announcing that a middling bride would do for the much-married Tudor king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' is a marriage partner: Catherine Parr was Henry VIII's sixth and last wife, and outlived him.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine of that surname married the Tudor king in 1543, so she was a marriage partner for him.

clue.text: Like the "organic harp diversely framed" of Coleridge

definitions.text: Like the "organic harp diversely framed" of Coleridge

parts.words: Like the "organic harp diversely framed" of Coleridge
parts.note: Coleridge's poem on the wind harp imagines all living things as organic harps diversely framed, so the clue asks for the harp's adjective

explanation.surface: A line borrowed from Coleridge about nature as a set of living harps.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's 'The Eolian Harp' (1795) asks 'what if all of animated nature / Be but organic Harps diversely framed'; such a harp is played by the wind, named for Aeolus, its god.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind harp takes its adjective from Aeolus, the Greek keeper of the winds, which is Coleridge's harp.

clue.text: Henry Brooke's deliverance

definitions.meaning: Henry Brooke, the 18th-century Irish writer, published a poem with this title in 1772
being saved or set free, especially from sin

explanation.surface: An Irish author's rescue from trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooke's religious poem bears this title, and the word means salvation or being set free from sin.

clue.text: Morning letter an audacious imposition in Plautus play

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is morning
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a try-on is a cheeky attempt to deceive or impose on someone

explanation.surface: A dawn note that brazenly takes advantage in a Roman comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try-on' is British slang for a bold attempt to get away with something.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman comedy by Plautus is named for the Theban general whose wife Jupiter seduces in his shape.

clue.text: A car for Madox at river crossing

definitions.meaning: the American carmaker founded by Henry, makers of the Model T
the novelist ... Madox ... shared his first name and surname
a shallow place where a river can be waded

explanation.surface: A motor for an author named Madox waiting at a shallow river.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names Henry's car company, the surname and forename of the author of The Good Soldier, and a shallow crossing.

clue.text: Gangster's girl on Belgian soil was a survivor

parts.note: a moll is a gangster's girlfriend
Flanders is the Dutch-speaking northern region of Belgium

explanation.surface: A gangster's girlfriend in the Belgian fields who lived to tell the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Defoe's heroine lives through poverty, many marriages, crime and transportation to Virginia, and ends prosperous: a survivor.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's 1722 heroine outlasts every hardship and ends her days rich and penitent, a model of endurance.

clue.text: Holy book put back in a devil's library

indicators.note: the found letters are read backwards, from right to left
the book's name is found inside the run of letters of a devil's library

explanation.surface: A sacred text returned to the shelves of Satan's own collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ADEV, the opening letters of 'a devil's', is turned round by 'put back'; 'library' looks like the definition's home but only hosts the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The four ancient Sanskrit scriptures of Hinduism carry this name, meaning knowledge.

clue.text: Golly, miss out in specious argument

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise from someone who has missed the flaw in a plausible case.
explanation.walkthrough: GOLLY MISS, rearranged as 'out' signals, gives the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument drawing a conclusion from two premises, and the word is also used of a clever but deceptive one.

clue.text: Conflict follows article on misdeed

indicators.note: in a down clue the article written on the misdeed sits below it
the conflict comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a crime is a misdeed
an is the indefinite article
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: A fight that breaks out after a wrongdoing is reported.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the 1853 to 1856 war was itself a conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: The war of 1853 to 1856 between Russia and an alliance of Britain, France and Turkey was fought on that peninsula.

clue.text: He wrote with Miss Edna in mind

definitions.text: He wrote with Miss Edna in mind

parts.words: He wrote with Miss Edna in mind
parts.note: a playwright said he wrote for an imagined middle-class matinee-goer he called Aunt Edna

explanation.surface: A writer who kept a particular woman in his thoughts as he worked.
explanation.walkthrough: Terence Rattigan, the English playwright of The Browning Version, invented 'Aunt Edna', a respectable lady theatregoer whose tastes he said a dramatist must satisfy.
explanation.definitionFit: The English playwright coined his imagined theatregoer 'Aunt Edna' in a 1953 preface and claimed to write for her.

clue.text: Boulle's had monkeys

parts.note: Pierre Boulle's novel is about a world ruled by apes

explanation.surface: A remark that a person named Boulle kept monkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: Boulle's novel was published in English as 'Planet of the Apes'; apes are loosely monkeys here.
explanation.definitionFit: Boulle's 1963 novel sets its story on a world ruled by apes, filmed in 1968.

clue.text: Laureate needed a star to steer her

definitions.text: Laureate needed a star to steer her

parts.words: Laureate needed a star to steer her
parts.note: a Poet Laureate's poem asks for a sailing vessel and a star to steer her by

explanation.surface: A prize-winner who required a star to guide her.
explanation.walkthrough: John Masefield, Poet Laureate, wrote in 'Sea Fever': 'And all I ask is a tall ship and a star to steer her by.'
explanation.definitionFit: Masefield's line asks for a large sailing vessel, and ships are 'her' in sailors' usage.

clue.text: Eliot's dock?

definitions.meaning: T. S. Eliot wrote a 1930 poem with this title, about Pericles finding his lost daughter
a harbour for yachts and pleasure boats

explanation.surface: Asking whether the poet Eliot owned a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliot's poem takes its title from Shakespeare's Pericles, and the word also means a basin for moored small boats.

clue.text: Burgoyne's was the first. Shakespeare's the second and third

definitions.text: Burgoyne's was the first. Shakespeare's the second and third

parts.words: Burgoyne's was the first. Shakespeare's the second and third
parts.note: General John Burgoyne wrote a libretto on the Lionheart, the first king of that name; Shakespeare wrote histories of the second and third

explanation.surface: A ranking that puts Burgoyne first and Shakespeare second and third.
explanation.walkthrough: Burgoyne adapted 'Richard Coeur de Lion' (1786) about Richard I; Shakespeare's history plays are Richard II and Richard III.
explanation.definitionFit: Three English kings bear the name: the Lionheart in Burgoyne's opera and the next two in Shakespeare's histories.

clue.text: Bear a nymph

definitions.meaning: the nymph was turned into a bear and set in the sky as the Great Bear
in Greek myth she was a nymph of Artemis seduced by Zeus

explanation.surface: Putting up with a nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: The huntress follower of Artemis was changed into a she-bear and placed among the stars as Ursa Major.

clue.text: Composer met in corpore sana

indicators.note: Latin for in the body, so one word goes inside the body of the other

explanation.surface: A composer encountered in a healthy body, echoing the Latin motto about a sound mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface twists Juvenal's 'mens sana in corpore sano'; 'in corpore' puts MET inside the body of SANA.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrich Smetana was the Czech composer of Ma Vlast and The Bartered Bride.

clue.text: Prepared for breakfast — article for Mrs Lawrence

parts.note: eggs and bacon are fried for breakfast
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Cooked in the morning, an item for D. H. Lawrence's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: D. H. Lawrence's wife was Frieda von Richthofen, who left her first husband for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Frieda von Richthofen married the novelist D. H. Lawrence in 1914 after eloping with him.

clue.text: Like some of Sharpe's old bad habits…

definitions.text: Like some of Sharpe's old bad habits

parts.words: Like some of Sharpe's old bad habits
parts.note: Tom Sharpe's comic novel is titled after vices inherited from forebears, old bad habits

explanation.surface: Describing the long-standing vices of a man named Sharpe.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Sharpe's 1980 satire is 'Ancestral Vices'; the vices are the old bad habits, and the adjective describes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Inherited from one's forebears, as the vices in Tom Sharpe's novel title are.

clue.text: …1It's Christmas for Streatfeild

definitions.meaning: a word for Christmas, seen on cards and in carols
the forename of the children's author of Ballet Shoes

explanation.surface: Christmas arrives for a person named Streatfeild.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word means Christmas, and it was also the forename of the author of Ballet Shoes.

clue.text: Words for detached spouse in race

indicators.note: the former spouse is placed inside the race

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
an ex is a former husband or wife

explanation.surface: Messages left for an estranged partner during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the Isle of Man's Tourist Trophy motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: The written words of a book or document make up its body of writing.

clue.text: Remembered by Trollope

parts.note: Thomas Adolphus Trollope, Anthony's elder brother

explanation.surface: Something the Victorian author Trollope recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trollope' looks like Anthony, but it is his brother Thomas Adolphus whose 1887 memoir is titled 'What I Remember'; the answer is the thing remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: The memoir's title begins with the pronoun for the thing recalled, so this word stands for whatever Trollope remembered.

clue.text: It lay beyond the great salt fount of tears, said Wilcox

definitions.text: It lay beyond the great salt fount of tears, said Wilcox

parts.words: It lay beyond the great salt fount of tears, said Wilcox
parts.note: Ella Wheeler Wilcox's poem names the garden of Christ's agony as the place everyone reaches past their tears

explanation.surface: A line from a poet named Wilcox about a place beyond an ocean of weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: Ella Wheeler Wilcox, the American poet, wrote 'Gethsemane', placing the garden where Jesus prayed before his arrest beyond the sea of tears.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden on the Mount of Olives where Jesus suffered before his arrest is the subject of Wilcox's poem.

clue.text: Dire version of Chiantishire poet

indicators.note: a version of a word is a reworking, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim translation of a poet from Tuscany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chiantishire' is the British nickname for Tuscany, popular with English holiday-makers; Francesco Redi wrote the Tuscan dithyramb 'Bacco in Toscana'.
explanation.definitionFit: Francesco Redi was a 17th-century Tuscan physician and poet, author of Bacco in Toscana.

clue.text: Graduate at university, getting by in French as novelist

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
passant is French for passing, going by

explanation.surface: A graduate at college managing to scrape by in French as a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting by' reads as coping, but it means passing by, which French says as passant.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy de Maupassant was the French short-story writer and novelist of Bel-Ami.
